I don't need to use that document at all. The first five documents are important to me. And this is the first time I hear of these names today. They are not in any of the previous documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: VS-1067, you testified that you were -- your unit was given an order to round up remaining Muslim and Croat civilians. From what area were they to be rounded up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area of Zalik. That's in Mostar, opposite the Northern Camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Would that be on the eastern or the western side of the river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The eastern side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And in your testimony earlier on today, a couple of times you made reference to events taking place on the right-hand side or the left-hand side of the river. Now, the right-hand side of the river, is that east or west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I say the right-hand side, then if we're going towards Sarajevo, it's the right side. But if we're going from Metkovic, it's the left side. However, we all say that the area where the Croats were is the right side, west bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So when you testified about the right side, you testified about an area that was predominantly Croat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's not correct that it was predominantly Croat, because the population was mixed there, all of us were a mixed population. However, above Mostar over there, the population was, I think, almost 100 per cent Croat. The town, itself, was not populated by Croats only.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like the usher if we can call up an exhibit that has already been admitted as P851.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: VS-1067, I'm going to ask you about the list which hopefully comes up in a bit. Can we zoom in on the top part? That will be fine. Can you see this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, because at -- you have talked about a friend of yours that you went to try to fetch. And at page 16, line 9, his spelling might not have been entirely correct. I wanted to ask you is: Your friend that you have testified about today, is he on this list, is his name there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. We're done with the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You talked about the junkyard, and could you describe the role that Rajko Janjic had in events there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rajko Janjic, well, he stood by a machine, a bulldozer. Later on, I heard that he used that bulldozer to cover the bodies of the dead. He was a bulldozer driver, otherwise-wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, later on people were talking about it, and he, himself, boasted about that, that he covered the bodies that way and was involved in that killing. He was involved in all sorts of things, at least according to the way he had talked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did he tell you how many people were killed at the junkyard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He didn't tell me exactly, but later on we heard on the news and people were saying that they had killed around 100 persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And we talked about the junkyard. What's the name of that or the name of the location where it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uborak, Uborak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you -- is it correctly spelled U-b-o-r-a-k?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did Janjic also tell you about other killings that took place on the 13th of June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He didn't tell me exactly. Well, he talked about all sorts of things when he would get drunk. To tell you the truth, I didn't even listen all the time. He said that he and Pejak would give two sheep for a Muslim, well, all sorts of rubbish. To tell you the truth, I didn't even listen to him, and I don't even know what he did say and what he did not say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a killing of some people at a location referred to as VTI?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they brought them there. There was a group there from Bjelusine, Seselj's men, and they took them for interrogations. And what they did to them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How do you know it was Seselj's men who took them there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean? Those who were there, the VTI. I mean, are you asking me how come I know who the people at the VTI were?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, these people came to Bjelusine, and there was a group there. It was sort of -- well, this was a military institute, and they had re-done it and it was sort of a pharmacy by then, and there were some wounded persons there. However, there were also members of the Serb Radical Party there who had come from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And how do you know that the members of the Serb Radical Party from Serbia were involved in the killing of the 30 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean at Uborak? I mean, you got me a bit confused now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: According to what you remember, what happened, and the VTI? Let's start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that they brought some people there. But that they killed him, I don't know, I can't remember. I mean, I'm so confused now. It's been 18 years, after all, Mr. Prosecutor. However, some members of the Serb Radical Party were there who had come from Serbia, and they were stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I understand, and thanks for being so open to the Court about what you remember and what you don't remember. That's, of course, very important. Are you familiar with or do you today remember --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's the Prosecutor testifying. How can he say whether it's sincere or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: VS-1067, are you familiar with an incident in which some people got killed in the woods in June 1992? Or, rather, maybe I should put that differently. Let me rephrase that. That some people were detained or rounded up in the woods and killed at someplace, 79 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Halfway between Mostar and Zijemlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Please explain to the Judges what you know about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were Muslims from Nevesinje. The police captured them, and also some volunteers from Serbia participated in that too. And I know that they said that they had killed all of them. The commander of the military police then was this Zdravko Kandic. Zdravko Kandic was commander of the military police in the Nevesinje Brigade then. This is -- well, on the 16th of June, the Army of Republika Srpska was established, and it happened around then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the usher to call up Exhibit 65 ter number 1771, please. And I'd like us to go to the last page of that. And if we can zoom in under the signature block or sort of the lower part of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I believe that this document is signed by a person called Krsto Savic, and it says "Chief of the Centre." Would this be the person that you have already mentioned with this name as chief of the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I just indicate to the Court that the document is signed for Mr. Savic. It's not his signature on the document, and that's reflected in the translation as well. Could we now call up 65 ter 1551, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. What does this mean, Judges? The witness mentioned Krsto Savic as the chief of police for that part of Herzegovina, and now the Prosecutor is showing a document to the witness, and on the last page of this document it says "Krsto Savic," but it also says that someone else signed this. Now, what is the Prosecutor doing to us in this courtroom? Krsto Savic is alive and healthy, is in prison in Bosnia, and at every point in time is accessible to the OTP and to the Court. You can summon him to testify here. But the Prosecutor is turning this trial into a mockery. What is the witness supposed to recognise here; that Krsto Savic's name is typewritten here and that somebody else signed on his behalf? Why is the Prosecutor doing this to us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, do you wish to reply or do we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I believe that I pointed out the very fact that the document wasn't signed by Mr. Savic. No attempt at misleading anyone here. The document is stamped, and it's quite normal that military and police documents and reports are signed by a lower-ranking officer on behalf of a superior officer. So there's nothing abnormal about this. I haven't even tendered the document yet. I might do that later, but let's see. Now, I asked if we could see 65 ter number 1551. So once we get that up, I believe, Your Honours, that this time we have a document which is signed by Mr. Savic, himself. No, that's incorrect. It's signed by Milorad Cuk this time for Mr. Savic. I'd like to go to page 5 of the English version and to page 5 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I insist that you first ask whether the witness ever had this document in his hands at the relevant time. This witness here is not a military or police expert, so he cannot testify about official documents. Krsto Savic can be asked about his document, or this assistant of his, Milorad Cuk, who signed on his behalf, not this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm going to have a question about the contents of the document, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this witness cannot give his opinion about the content of the document. The witness is testifying about what he had seen or heard. He's not supposed to give his opinion about the content of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the witness has never seen this document, that's for sure, but the document mentions a number of items, which you will see, which cross-reference what he said before. Let the Prosecutor put his question, and during your cross-examination you'll be able to provide counter evidence. On looking at the document, I see that there are some paragraphs which coincide with what he has said already. Please proceed, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Towards the top of the document, there's a description of a group of people as Seselj's men, and then there's talk about leader called Vranjanac. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when this Mico Drazic left, he represented himself as their leader, and he did not disarm in August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And he presented himself as the leader of who, of what group, of who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the leader of this group of Seselj's men, and they all obeyed him. As I've already said, they mistreated people. It didn't matter whether you were Serb, Croat, or a Muslim. They maltreated everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would at this point tender Exhibit 65 ter 1551. The witness has clearly corroborated the contents of the document, and we also have learned from the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Let me finish my submission on why the document should be admitted, then you can answer afterwards. And the witness has --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You interrupt me, too. When I speak, you interrupt me, you intervene, and then I stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Prosecutor is explaining why he wishes to tender it into evidence. Let him finish, and then you can object. He hasn't finished. What did you want to say, Mr. Marcussen? You wanted to tender --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I was going to seek the admission of 65 ter 1551. The witness has confirmed that the person who at least is put on as being the authority who issued the document that is stamped is, in fact, a person who had the position that the document says, and the witness has confirmed the correctness or corroborated the correctness of the information in the document. And I submit that on that basis, the document is admissible, and I tender it before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, what did you have to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is absolutely impossible. This witness is testifying about what happened in Mostar. Milorad Cuk describes what happened in Nevesinje. The witness, himself, says that Vranjanac was expelled with his group in October 1992 in Nevesinje. Then someone should explain to us how come this group came to Nevesinje and they appeared in Mostar. What does that mean, that it was in Mostar? How come? It is Krsto Savic or Milorad Cuk that can explain that. And you keep saying that various gangs were affiliated with me. Even if they did introduce themselves as Seseljevci, call someone who is competent and then admit it into evidence. I cannot question this witness about a document that Cuk signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's give this document an MFI number, and the Chamber will deliberate after the examination. Can we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P891, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a follow-up question. This document seems to be an official document. It is a report on the activities of paramilitary formations, and in this document there is mention of a group called Seselj's men, led by Vranjanac. You said that this leader was in command until August 1992, and you said that they were expelled after that. Very well. But you added something in passing, but which I believe was of utmost importance. Just look at the transcript. You said that these people, as the document says, were carrying out abuse, they were abusing Muslims, Croats, and Serbs, which could mean that this group was also attacking the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, they didn't attack them with weapons, but they mistreated them and abused them. There is this one thing that happened before their expulsion from Nevesinje. They mined the Croatian church in Nevesinje. Look at this paradox. The Croatian church is practically in the center of town. Twenty metres away, there are residential houses, and also nearby is a hospital where there were 150 to 200 wounded were put up there. And imagine, when they blew up that church, how damaged the houses and the hospital were. And that led to the elimination of these people from there, because they blew up this Croatian church in the middle of an inhabited settlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Marcussen, proceed. I believe you have less than 15 minutes left, maybe only 10 minutes or 5 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could we call up -- sorry. Maybe we could call up 65 ter number 1771 again. And if we can go to page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, what exactly is this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This is a report signed for Krsto Savic from the Security Centre of the Republika Srpska, Ministry of Interior, and it is a report on the work of the Trebinje CSB, so that will be the Security Centre, on the period from April to December 1992, so the time-frame that's relevant to the allegations in the indictment. And they talk about the establishment of the RS MUP in the area, and it's relevant for that reason to the case, as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What I wanted to ask, VS-1067, is: There is mention of some special units of the police in some -- it will be in the third paragraph in the B/C/S version of what you are seeing. Are you familiar with Special Police units being in any of these locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Seselj, you have one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In these statements of yours and during today's testimony, I was surprised by many things, but I was most surprised when you said that my associates contacted you and disturbed you and threatened you. So when the Presiding Judge asked you which of my associates, you mentioned Dragan Samardzic and Drago Tamindzija; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How do you know that those two men are my associates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about Samardzic. But Drago Tamindzija, when the war ended, he was one of the main people in the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, during the break my people contacted Nevesinje and learned that Dragan Samardzic has been living abroad for quite some time and that it isn't known whether he's a member of any party. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it could be. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you didn't say he was a member, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said that he was an associate of mine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say -- well, he called me up and threatened me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly speak one at a time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Judge asked you which of my associates called you up, and you mentioned him first. Now, I don't want to enter into whether he actually threatened you or not. I have no interest in challenging that. All I want to know is: Did you say he was my associate or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A moment ago, you expressly stated that he was my associate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know about Drago Tamindzija for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mean that he was my associate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he was in your party in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In 1996, he was, but he called you in 2007 and threatened you. That's what you said; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From your party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You speak the same language, so you fall into the trap of overlapping, which makes it impossible for the interpreters to interpret and thus communicate to us what you're saying. So please observe a pause between answer and question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that since 2002, in Republika Srpska there is a party which is called the Serbian Radical Alliance of Dr. Vojislav Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that there exists a political party who is falsely representing itself as the Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I've heard of the existence of that party.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, would you be so kind -- well, yes, I am switching off my microphone as soon as I finish, I am taking that on board. Now, could we provide the witness with this copy, and I hope that you have distributed it to the Trial Chamber and to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, with your help, let's establish who this Drago Tamindzija is. The first document is an official copy of the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska, and it speaks about certified lists -- nomination lists for 2004, the 20th of October, 2004. Now, turn over -- the 2nd of October, rather. And then you'll see the parties in Nevesinje that are up for election, and it says that there's this Serbian Radical Alliance of Dr. Vojislav Seselj, and it says that's in the middle of the page, second column in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then a little lower down it says "The Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska"; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now turn the page -- or, rather, don't go on to the next page right away. On the page we were dealing with, it says "The Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska." That is the party which falsely represented itself as being the Radical Party; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I really can't say. If it says "The Serbian Radical Party" here, and I can't comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says the "Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Before that, it said "The Serbian Radical Alliance of Dr. Vojislav Seselj" in column 3, can you see that? And can you see the list of nominees in Nevesinje beginning with Dragan Vistic [phoen], Natasa Mustic [phoen], Luka Radojcic [phoen], et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now here we have "The Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska," as it says. Now, if a party bears my name in its title, then it did so to be clearly differentiated from some false party with a similar name; is that logical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, this Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska which I say is falsely representing itself has as its candidate -- as its nominee Drago Tamindzija; is that right? Turn the page, and you will see name underlined, and it is "Drago Tamindzija"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So Drago Tamindzija is a candidate in the elections of this party that falsely represents itself as a radical party which I don't recognise as being our party, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now turn to the next page. It's another document, and here we have the electoral results for Nevesinje Municipality, the local elections held in 2008?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says "The Serbian Radical Party, Dr. Vojislav Seselj"; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And we won 826 votes or 12.15 per cent; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Right below that is the "Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska," and it secured 7.46 per cent of the votes; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are those two different parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From this document, we can see that they are, indeed, two different parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, examining a witness last week, I said that this other party falsely representing itself was led by Mihajlo Mihajlica. Do you know this man, Mihajlo Mihajlica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, turn to the next page, and it's document number 3 that I'd like to look at now. It is the Nevesinje Municipal Assembly, and we have the electoral results there. The Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska, that's the one that I don't recognise and doesn't have my name in its heading; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So everything is clear now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And number 5 is Drago Tamindzija; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now turn to the next page, which is document number 4, and these are elections in 2004. It says, "The Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska," and in fourth place "Drago Tamindzija," right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now turn to the next page, and this is document 5. Once again, we have the elections for the Municipal Assembly of Nevesinje Municipality, and this is the Serbian Radical Alliance of Vojislav Seselj; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There we have a list of candidates and who was elected and Drago Tamindzija is no where on the list, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And document number 6, I'm not going to ask you anything about that. It's an application form for Radovan Radovic becoming a member of the Serbian Radical Party. Have I convinced you here now that Drago Tamindzija cannot be an associate of mine in any way and that he's not a member of the party that I lead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, but when you say "Serbian Radical Party," nobody abroad, we all think that it's -- they're your men. I had no idea that this Serbian Radical Alliance of Vojislav Seselj existed and the BH Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, now it's clear to you that a party does exist which is registered as being the Serbian Radical Party, but that it is erroneously presenting itself. And is it possible that in the war, you might have come across people who falsely represented themselves as being Seselj's men; is that possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And is it possible that this man, Vranjanac, is one of those people who was expelled from Nevesinje for crime and false representation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is possible, sir. But if you would like me to give you some elements, to have the man arrested and then an investigation can be launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecutor can give orders for that. I haven't started arresting anybody yet, and if I do, well, all hell will break lose one day, if one day I start arresting people, unless they keep me here in prison for the rest of my life. Now, you mentioned the arrival of Seselj's men in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that's true. A group of volunteers, at the beginning of April, 7th or 8th of April, 1992, did indeed arrive in Mostar, and it was put up next to the command of General Perisic, is that right, next to his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them in Bjelusine the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was Perisic's command there somewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Perisic's command and headquarters was somewhere in North Camp, or I'm not sure exactly, or at the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You were in North Camp, and Perisic wasn't there. Just let me finish. I haven't got much time. I'd like to get through all this. I will have some blitz questions to ask you. You said that they arrived in three trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Which direction did they arrive from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the south, from Buna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is that from the airport direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that they came to Mostar by plane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they have absolutely brand-new camouflage uniforms, the likes of which nobody had seen in Mostar until then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down. It's impossible to translate at this speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Slow down, please. You speak too fast, and it's impossible for the interpreters to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So during April, these volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, so-called Seselj's men, it was easy to recognise them because they were wearing new camouflage uniforms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, since the beginning of May the camouflage uniforms were given to other members of the JNA, the Territorial Defence and other units; is that true too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's like this, let me tell you: People did have them, but 95 per cent were wearing the olive-green-type uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But in May, supplies of camouflage uniforms started. That's all the information I need you to confirm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the military police begin to wear these camouflage uniforms, too, at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military police and the reconnaissance men, they had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They began wearing them first, when we're talking about the Serb forces, because it was still the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So when they began wearing camouflage uniforms, you were no longer able to distinguish Seselj's men from the rest; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Seselj's men all had long beards. They didn't shave. So those who represented themselves as being your men, they had long hair and beards and never shaved. We, of course, did shave.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that I am the oldest Chetnik vojvoda to this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I respect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that I've never had long hair or a long beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So why would this wearing of long beards be a mark of Seselj's men? Do you know that there were other men, too, who kept the Chetnik tradition of wearing long beards from different parties and so on; Vuk Draskovic and et cetera? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that Vuk Draskovic, at Ravno Gora, erected the first monument to Draza Mihajlovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So I don't have the monopoly over the Serbian Chetnik Movement; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. There are other groups, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it true that the Serb adversaries called all Serb forces, referred to them as Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they call you Chetniks, the Muslims, Croats and so on, did they call you Chetniks too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you mentioned the Serbian Chetnik Movement here in Nevesinje of Arsen Grahovac. Now, do you know that Arsen Grahovac was a member of the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Chetnik Movement within our composition, so our constitutive part, in actual fact, constituent part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think he used to say he was a Vukovac man, a Vuk man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you have no proof that he has anything to do with the Serbian Radical Party and me personally and the Chetnik Movement within our composition, under us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they had their own Karadjordje Chetnik Movement, and to whom they belonged, I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, the authorities of the Muslim-Croatian federation arrested you sometime in 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were accused of some war crime, but you were released from prison quickly and you were given a symbolic sentence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I spent three and a half months in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, in the -- during the investigation, you gave a statement, and in that statement you described this crime at Zalik, Vrapcici, and so on, where, on two occasions, more than 100 Muslims were killed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The statement you gave to the Muslim authorities served the Cantonal Prosecutor's Office in Mostar to expand the indictment against people who personally took part in that crime; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What happened, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was accused, as well as Sasa Zurovac. Sasa Vaskovic [phoen] and Matkovic were accused of having killed some Muslim civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's leave that to one side, why you were accused. You were accused for a limited number of killings; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Two or three or four?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But when you made your statement to the Muslim-Croatian federation authorities and then an investigating judge, you described this crime in detail at Uborak and Zijemlje and what happened at the football statement at Vrapcici? You told them the story in great detail; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that was recorded, your testimony was recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's what was -- what should have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you name the names of people whom you knew had taken part in the crime; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There were some 14 or 15 people that you mentioned, that you named; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do you know that the Cantonal Prosecution Office from Mostar raised an indictment against some 30 Serbs for these crimes in Zijemlje, at Uborak, and in Vrapcici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I showed this document here in the courtroom. I was provided it by the Prosecutor. And all those people on the list were accused of something, whether in Mostar or in the surrounding municipalities, but you have no knowledge of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you made your statement to the Muslim authorities or, rather, the authorities of the federation, nowhere did you mention Seselj's men, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mentioned those people, but I didn't know their names, their first and last names. There was a Vranjanac, there was a Srecko, a Bosanac, and so on. Now why they didn't take them I don't know, but I did mention them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Judges, the OTP was duty-bound to disclose that statement by this witness in the Mostar investigation and then they failed to do so. All I have is a copy of the judgement, where we can see that this witness was given a very mild sentence and released from prison or, rather, exchanged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was exchanged after three and a half months.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were exchanged for some Muslims that were supposed to be tried in Republika Srpska. So, Judges, that was tendentious on the part of the OTP for failing to provide me with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, the next statement that you gave, you gave in a foreign country where you were arrested for theft, as you, yourself, told us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I am just discovering that you were in jail for three and a half months. You hadn't mentioned this in your statements -- in your 2004 statement, and that you had been indicted for murder.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2006, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that you were indicted for the murder of two to three people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two people. In the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there are investigating judges and investigators, and these are professional people, generally speaking. Were you heard by the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, an investigating judge interrogated me. However, these two civilians who were referred to, they were members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they had the insignia of the golden lily, the highest in their army. However, the other people were civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All the better for you, it's what's most important for you. But when the investigative judge put questions to you about these crimes and those who had committed the crimes or committed -- or participated in the crimes, why didn't you mention paramilitary groups at the moment, including Seselj's men? Why didn't you mention that at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean, when I was in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did not mention Seselj's men at that point, Judge. He mentioned the perpetrators of the crime by their names, but he did not mention Seseljevci at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking you for the following reason: An investigative judge is a professional, a senior professional, and normally when this man investigates a crime, he wants to know the ins and outs of the crime. So when speaking with you, he puts a question, and he probably wanted to know who committed these crimes and whether these formations reported to or belonged to political parties. I assume he asked these questions, but I don't have the transcripts here, but it seems that you never mentioned Seselj's men except in 1998, when you were asked questions by the investigator of the OTP. I'm trying to understand why, in a very serious investigation, in front of a professional judge, you said nothing, but later on you provide details, but only later on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, sir. I repeated the same thing in Mostar, what I'm saying here and now. Now, it wasn't the judge who was putting questions to me; it was policemen. I just go to the judge, who'd read something out to me, and then I'd go away. Perhaps I'd spend 15 minutes with the judge, 15 or 20 minutes. Is that enough to clarify a war crime?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever the case may be, you said that you mentioned Seselj's men in front of the policeman who conducted the investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, now this is a new thing for me as well. As for this statement before a Muslim Croatian policeman, I never received it, and I was supposed to receive all of that, all the previous statements made by this witness that the Prosecutor has, and the Prosecution did not submit that to me on purpose. Now, only 23 days ago --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It's now the third time that the accused is alleging that we have been holding back documents from him. We have disclosed the documents we have. It is well known to the Court and it's well known to the accused that there might be occasion when witnesses have given statements to other authorities which the Prosecution don't have. The accused should refrain from this. We have disclosed, to the best of my knowledge, everything we have regarding the witness. The accused has his own large team who can go and get the documents that needs -- wants for his examination, so I object to these kind of allegations against the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, this is what I had understood. Seemingly, the Prosecutor did not receive these documents. He is telling you that he has given you everything he has. The interview before the investigating judge and the policeman is something which he did not receive. He might not even have known about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to deny that. What I received here is a copy of the judgement against this witness in 1996. Where there is the copy of the judgement, there is also a witness statement made by him, at the beginning, then from the investigation itself, and also the statement given before the police. The Prosecution provided me with only a copy of the judgement, because there is nothing in the judgement. And now where there is some content and what is important for me is what the Prosecution is not giving me. Now it seems they are trying to present it as if I had a stronger team than the OTP. That is ridiculous, Judges, that I have more resources than the OTP. How can I have contacts with the police or the judiciary of the federation? I have no contacts with them whatsoever. I can have contacts with people from Nevesinje, people who lived in Mostar up until the war, and so on and so forth. As for the official authorities of the federation, I have no contact whatsoever with them. The OTP does have contacts with them and has good co-operation with them, and they didn't want to provide me with these documents. And they knew that these documents had to exist, even though they claim that they do not have them in their hands, which I do not believe. May I continue now? On the 29th of January, the OTP informed me of the following, and they submitted to me the police report of a foreign country from 1998. Oh, please don't tell me that the OTP received it only on the 29th of January 2010, that they received that police report, that -- they got it a lot earlier. This police report was a pretext for The Hague investigators to interview this witness at all in late 1998. Otherwise, they wouldn't have known of this witness, had the police of that foreign country arrested -- not arrested them -- him, rather. I'm not going to mention the name of the country, otherwise, you'll redact the transcript. Should I go on or are we going to wait for Mr. Marcussen to go on whispering? All right, then let me move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In 1998, you were arrested in a foreign country, and that is where you were interviewed on account of different kinds of theft; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Also the crime of driving without a license, possession of weapons, and so on, all sorts of things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When the police completed those interviews, then they started interrogating you about the war, and you described very precisely everything that happened on the 13th of June, 1992, in the area of Vrapcici, Uborak, Zijemlje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And there you mentioned the names of the perpetrators of those crimes; that is, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 -- at least 12 names; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You described all of that in detail, and you did not mention at all that there was a single man of Seselj's there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Seselj. Mr. Marcussen, I have a question for you. I'm discovering that you disclosed at the beginning of January to Mr. Seselj this report that has to do with the events that he is charged with in this foreign country. This witness is a witness of the Court. Why didn't you give this to the Judges, for what reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The order that we were given was to provide the Chamber with all statements of the witnesses. That is what we were -- we were given some additional directions, for example, not to provide transcripts of witnesses who have testified, only their statements. There was some material that had already been provided to the Chamber. And so that is what we have done. This witness has criminal record. They have been disclosed to the accused. And, actually, the information that the accused just made reference to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, let me stop you here. I acknowledge that you have not disclosed documents which, in my view, should have been disclosed because these documents have to do with the character of the witness. Don't forget that he has protective measures, that in this document he has made statements about the events that took place in June of 1992, and these documents are documents which I do not have. That's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The statements that the accused is making reference to, I have already explained, we have disclosed everything we had, the statements that we would have had from the witness from other authorities would also have been given to Your Honours, pursuant to your order, for your remaining witnesses. The criminal records have not been provided to you because we did not realise the Chamber wanted this. All this kind of material has been disclosed to the accused under Rule 68, and actually the information that I think the accused is referring to that he got on the 29th of January was provided to him back when the witness was originally scheduled to testify in the form of a proofing note, that we disclosed to the accused as soon as the information came out, and the witness had told us about this information in proofing. We had then obtained the official records, we have had them translated from a foreign language and into the accused's language, and we have only been able to disclose on the 29th to the accused. So I strongly object to these allegations of any impropriety and deliberate delays in the Prosecution's disclosure of any material to the accused. It's simply unfounded. It's repeated allegations by the accused, and it's inappropriate. Now, if Your Honours would like to receive this kind of information with respect to the remaining witnesses, I am happy to undertake to go back and look at what other criminal records we may have for some of these witnesses. I am aware that we have disclosed documents in that regard to the accused, and I'm happy to provide them to the Chamber. We're certainly not trying to hold anything back from Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What Mr. Marcussen said is an absolute lie. The first time the police record of an interrogation of this witness before the police of a foreign country from July 1998, I received it for the first time on the 29th of January, 2010. It wasn't the beginning of January. That may have been misinterpreted to you. It was towards the end of January, the 29th of January. And today is the 3rd of February, so it was only this Friday that I first got this ever in my life, this Friday. And it's not true that it was given to me after the proofing. During the proofing, they did mention that the witness had been arrested, but as for the statement made before the police of this foreign country, I got it only now, and you never received it. However, I never received the statement made before the police in Mostar and before the investigating judge of the Muslim-Croat federation. I never received that. I simply do not have that. However, I do have information, that I received through a certain lawyer, that I was never mentioned in those two statements. In those two Mostar statements, there is no mention of Seseljevci. There is only mention of the persons who, to the best of the knowledge of this witness, who took part in the crimes that I am being charged with now. That is the core of the matter. May I proceed now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you denying that this is what you had said to the police of that foreign country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You enumerated the names of all the perpetrators that you allegedly knew of, the perpetrators of that crime in the area of Vrapcici, Zijemlje, and Uborak; you said that to the police of this foreign country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All of these are names of locals either from Mostar or from Nevesinje, and even now, if they live in a foreign country, you mentioned which foreign country they live in, right? You even put that there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember that. I can't remember that, but I know and I'm sure that I said that Bosanac, Srecko, were there, and that they said that they were Serb Radicals.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They are not in this document. Please, Judges, have a look at this document of the police of this foreign country and see for yourselves that these people are not there, that this witness is trying to present as Seseljevci only subsequently at a later point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you are talking about a document which the Prosecutor did not disclose to the Judges because he felt it was not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I suggest that we admit that -- that we put that document onto the record so everyone can see what it is that's being talked about. So why don't we admit it as a Defence exhibit or as a trial exhibit and then everyone can see it, and then no secrets. We're certainly not trying to hold back anything from the Judges. I strongly object to this. And as I've indicated, if there's anything the Judges would like to have from us, we are happy to share it with the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, not a single document that the OTP disclosed to me is going to be admitted into evidence as a Defence document. However, you ordered the OTP to provide you with all the statements of this witness, and they did not do that. Now, this statement before the police of a foreign country, they had it -- the OTP had it, and they didn't submit it to me -- to you, and they didn't submit to you or to me the statements made before the police in Mostar and the investigating judge in Mostar, which I think would be very, very important. I believe that's not in dispute. And now the Prosecutor is teaching me what I'm going to tender as Defence exhibits? I am not going to tender anything. I -- what matters to me is the public and that I show the public that I have cut into pieces this false indictment, and I did that from one witness to another. You have falsified the evidence, you forged the evidence, you have false witnesses, and all of that serves your purposes. Perhaps the Judges could save more time by not questioning this witness, and then I wouldn't have to do all of this for the sake of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You cannot say that the Prosecutor has forged an indictment which has been approved by the Judges, as you know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. All right, then. Then I forged everything. I forged the transcript, the police record from a police of a foreign country, and I stole it from the OTP, and then the OTP took for granted my forgery. I accept that. And I also forged the police record of this witness before the police in Mostar and before the investigating judge in Mostar. Right. Now, if you'll allow me to proceed. Let us try to get this done and over with today. Further questions are actually pointless, after what has happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, I received here from the Prosecutor quite a record of yours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since the OTP provided me with that, I would not have dealt with it, I really wouldn't have looked into your record or your CV, because I know what my volunteers did in that area. And if somebody had introduced themselves falsely, then there has to be material evidence to support that. I have proof. Have you heard of Oliver Denis Baret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the commander of the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party, the so-called Seseljevci, but the real original Seseljevci in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If Oliver Denis Baret was commander, no doubt about that, of the original Seseljevci in Mostar, then it couldn't have been Mico Drazic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sort of.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vranjanac came to the fore only in June, when Mico Drazic and Oliver whatever his name is disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Mico Drazic have anything to do with Oliver?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never saw them together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you heard that Oliver Denis Baret was commander of the Seseljevci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the OTP forbid you to put that into your statement when you talked to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oliver Denis Baret is a very well known name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well known?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come he's not mentioned in any one of your statements here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't mention him because I don't know of him creating any kind of problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You never heard of Oliver Denis Baret and people under his command taking part in any kind of crime; theft, looting, killing, any kind of crime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Any kind of crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you. This is very important to me, because I'm very proud of the role that Oliver Denis Baret and his people played in the war. Now, I have evidence here that Oliver Denis Baret withdrew from Mostar before the 25th. Actually, he withdrew together with the JNA. Do you know when the JNA left Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 28th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oliver Denis Baret withdrew before the 25th of May, and here he is at a rally that I held on the 25th of May in Podgorica. Podgorica is the capital of Montenegro; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that a shell had been thrown at me then in -- a hand-grenade had been thrown at me in Podgorica then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And here is the entire court record of the proceedings against the assassins. Sixty-two persons were wounded on that occasion. Did you hear that a large number of people were wounded there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that I was injured then as well, that I was hit in the leg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here we have, on page 50 -- I hope that the Prosecutor has found this. This is the interrogation of -- or, rather, the interview of Oliver Denis Baret as one of the wounded persons there. He was hit by 42 shrapnel. Do you know how many a hand-grenade has?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Perhaps 3.000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many. I don't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But it's an enormous number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I was wounded myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that one of my escorts was composed and that he kicked one of them under a car, that this saved several lives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And all of us who were wounded were wounded in the lower part of the abdomen or on our legs and feet; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you believe now that Oliver Denis Baret, on the 25th of May, was seriously wounded in Podgorica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if you have proof that he was in hospital, then I believe that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Forty-two balls were found in his body, and the Prosecution has that evidence and has had it for quite some time. Now, what the OTP provided me, as far as you're concerned, some other West European countries are mentioned where you were arrested. There were several others. We're not going to mention them. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was it four or five countries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Which others? No, all right. We're not going to mention countries. Right. So two more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A total of two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see, a total of two. And now they go on to list the reasons for which you were arrested. You were accused of having taken part in some crime organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Then something else listed here is what you stole. You stole in department stores mostly; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Clothing; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And all the items of clothing are listed. And then it says "Illegal possession of weapons," and then you were a suspect in a killing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And is all that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was just a suspect, but you don't spend just one month in prison if you have killed someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, I have information saying that during the war you were arrested in Nevesinje too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they were crimes of aggravated theft. And in addition to you, five more individuals were arrested, five others. We're not going to mention their names, not to disclose your identity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says that in the Nevesinje Municipality in 1993/1994, you looted several facilities, catering establishments, that you stole cameras, video-recorders, white goods, alcohol, coffee, cigarettes, and the like. Is it true that you were arrested for those reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just for the theft of various apparatuses and cameras.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I have this document from 1994 provided to me by the Prosecutor, but they failed to provide me with the police files and court files, and they were duty-bound to do so, Judges, to disclose to me everything that would help me challenge the credibility of this witness. You know that better than I do. You're far more better acquainted with the law than I am. I have just become acquainted with Defence counselling of late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to spend much time on this, but you were arrested for a series of thefts. Were you convicted or were you proved not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was a suspect, but never convicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to the information I have, belong to the Cicciolina unit; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it takes its name from Cicciolina, the famous Italian lady politician?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was a respected member of the Italian Parliament. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I need that for a bit of an exotic approach to these proceedings. Now, when you say that Seselj's men looted in Mostar and Nevesinje, you have in mind this man Vranjanac, I assume.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you have information according to which Oliver Denis Baret and his group ever stole anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oliver and his group, I didn't see them, but I did see this man, Vranjanac, and the other one. They took everything they could lay their hands on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'd like, the Prosecutor to identify this man, Vranjanac; if nothing else, then to accuse him of false representation here, because I can't seem to gather information about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then you say at one place that the stolen goods from Mostar were driven to Nis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere in Serbia. I don't know whether Nis in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your statement, it says "Nis."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I can find it. I'll take a moment, and maybe I can find it. Now, if you set out from Mostar to Nis in a truck, where would you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You'd go to Bjelica -- you'd pass through Bjelica, Niksic, Podgorica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Through Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you'd have to drive the stolen goods through Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that throughout Serbia there were police check-points, and throughout Montenegro you couldn't move from one town to another with clandestine goods or stolen goods without passing through check-points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise to you, Mr. Seselj, but from the Mostar Aluminium Company they took 300 trucks -- truckloads of aluminium. So how could they cross the borders? They had some papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mean Seselj's men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no, I mean the JNA. Perhaps they had some JNA documents or whatever. They had to have had some documents to be able to exit Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But for something to be transported from Mostar and Nevesinje to Serbian Montenegro, a large-scale mafia-type organisation must have existed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You couldn't just have a group of people loading goods up onto a truck and drive it away to Serbia and Montenegro without having a broader organisation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So do you agree that it was only the mafia that could smuggle goods on this scale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, sir. I don't know what documents they had, but they had to have some kind of permit from Mr. Perisic to be able to leave Herzegovina at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: War booty is one thing. If aluminium was an important strategic natural resource, the JNA took it from the aluminium combine or it took weapons from underground storehouses and depots? If it was tragically important, they could do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But what about people looting white goods and television sets and drive them to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, but they drove them off somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, they drove them off and then resold them to refugees in Nevesinje. And you said that 30.000 people had -- that there were 30.000 refugees from the Neretva River Valley, and they needed household goods in a hurry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So for somebody to drive white goods, used television sets, to Serbia, at that time it would be more costly to pay for the fuel needed for the trucks to drive these goods off than they would get by selling the goods, themselves; am I right in thinking along those lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So is there any logic, then, that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party who had come from Serbia, and only two groups arrived in that area, Oliver Denis Baret, one group, to the withdrawal of the JNA, and later on a small group of some 20 men under the command of Branislav Vakic in Nevesinje? Have you heard of Branislav Vakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So as to this group that was the regular volunteer group of the Serbian Radical Party, you've never heard of that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, we've logically established that the goods, used goods, white goods, it just didn't pay to have them transported that far away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it's true that you could sell them in Nevesinje for very little money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A television set costs 50 or 100 German marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So going very cheap. And unfortunately that's what happened during this war, theft and the resale of stolen goods, but it wasn't cost effective to take it all the way to Serbia and sell it there? Anyway, I have some more information that I'd like to deal with here. You said that some people killed a Croat, threw him into a shaft, and threw a hand-grenade after him and killed him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do you link those people to this man Vranjanac or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Vranjanac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what about Oliver Denis Baret; you definitely don't tie them up with him, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We had a witness in here before you who said that some Albanian had killed this Croat, throwing a hand-grenade into the shaft after him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that could be true, too, because there were several Albanians in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you couldn't say for sure -- identify for sure the person who killed that civilian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew who took him off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mentioned the Muslim village of Topla. The looting and setting fire to houses in that village, has it got anything to do with Oliver Denis Baret and the unit he was in command of? Just tell me yes or no so we can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you absolutely certain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. Do you know that some locals would get together, forming a band or gang of some kind, and say that they are members of some military formation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were examples of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know about Ratko Mladic's order from the summer of 1992, saying that all those units should be disarmed, arrested, or, if they had not committed any crimes, be incorporated into the regular Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, the paramilitaries. Now, do you know that the policy of the Serbian Radical Party, of which I was the head, was always against the formation of paramilitary formations and including all the fighters into the regular Army of Republika Srpska or, rather, Srpska Krajina, or, rather, the JNA, that I was opposed to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but those -- Vranjanac and the others who introduced themselves that way, I can't describe them to you. They were real idiots, madmen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. But do you have any evidence that this man, Vranjanac, and the people that he controlled I sent from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what they said, that's what they said, that you had sent them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They referred to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But they had no documents or papers or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had the little booklets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What did they look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were small blue booklets like an ID card, like the former Yugoslav ID cards used to be, a small booklet, navy blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you see whose signature was on the book? What did it say in those little booklets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You didn't; right. How much more time have I got, Judges?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe you have about 20 minutes left. We can continue until 10 to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then we can finish everything today, and I'll speed up a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you have any problems with the law before the war? For hooliganism, there was something of that nature; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, hooliganism, brawls among supporters, sports fans.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Some people told me that it was your custom to demolish vehicles with license plates from other towns.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the Hajduk football team supporters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When they come into Mostar to play against Velez; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know Boris Kozul, Toza, at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Edin Music, nicknamed Edin Muce, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He's not Edin Music, he's Edin Ramadanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. The interpreter didn't catch the next name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Sasa Zurovac? I think my microphone was off, but Sasa Zurovac, and the witness said, Yes. Did you know these people well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you socialise with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.
